SPECIFICATION FOR AMBADI OIL 0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 July 1979, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 In India, ambadi is cultivated mainly as a fibre crop in dry regions. Ambadi oil is obtained from seeds of ambadi Hibiscus cannabinus Linn. and Hibiscus sabdariffa Linn. var Altissima or a mixture of these seeds both belonging to fam. Malvaceae. The principal producing areas of ambadi in the country are Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Orissa. Its common Indian names are Ambari, Patsan, Pitwa and La1 Ambari. Its other names in English are Ambari hemp, Bimili, Deccan hemp, Jamaica, Roselle hemp, Sorrel, etc. 0.3 So far ambadi has been accepted only as a fibre crop but from latest scientific developments it has been found that the fibre quality will not impair much even if seed is allowed to set. The fibre still can be used for pulp and other industries. Thus the crop can be grown for both seeds as well as fibre. The potential for annual availability of ambadi seeds in the country is around 7.5 000 tonnes and around 13 000 tonnes of the ambadi oil. 0.4 Ambadi seeds contain 18 to 22 percent of oil. The seed has good storage stability and is tetrahedral in shape with strongly adherent coat The seed is flaked, cooked by steam difficult to separate from kernel. Residual oil in the and the oil is obtained by the process of expression. Alternatively, cake can be extracted with hexane. ambadi seeds, after crushing, cooking and flaking can be extracted directly with solvent. The yield of ambadi oil from its seeds by expression process is about 15 percent. The oil can be used for various industrial purposes. IConsidering shortage of oils in the country and the need to utilize indigenous resources of this oilseed, the concerned technical committee decided to formulate this specification. 0.5 This standard contains clause the purchaser and the supplier.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes test for ambadi oil. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, IS : 548 ( Part I )-1964t shall apply. 3. TYPES 3.1 The material shall be of the following two types: a) Expressed, and b) Solvent extracted. 4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Description - The material shall be obtained from good quality ambadi cake or from clean and sound seeds of ambadi Hibiscus cannabinus Linn. and Hibiscus sabdariffa Linn. var Altissimma or a mixture of these seeds, both belonging to fam. Malvaceae by a process of solventextraction or from ambadi seeds by a process of expression. 4.1.1 Solvent extracted oil shall be obtained from the seed kernels using solvent hexane conforming to IS : 3470-l 966:.

4.3 Admixture with Other Oils - The material shall be free from admixture with mineral or other oils of vegetable or animal origin, when tested according to the methods prescribed in IS : 548 ( Part II )-1976*.
NOTE - Ambadi oil like some other oils, namely, cotton seed, hempseed, kapok, etc, contains cyclopropene acids and hence gives positive Halphen test.
